_about: Replies to the live k-0535 reading prompt (intent.record.test.ts), recorded 2026-11-24 with Claude Haiku via claude -p (no tools, system prompt = the prompt + shape hint). The studio's own provider is Gemini/Mentor; the prompt is the same. Re-record after changing the prompt.

replies.en-10: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[1],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"B is not wrong. It is the answer key. Using the midpoint method, %ΔP = 2/11 ≈ 18.2% and %ΔQ = 10/95 ≈ 10.5%, so PED ≈ 0.58, which is less than 1 and therefore inelastic. Option A is wrong because PED is below 1, C would need PED exactly 1, and D would need no change in quantity at all.","picks":[]}
replies.en-11: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[2],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"Draft 2 asks for the price elasticity of supply between $4 and $6, which is a standard calculation skill in the HKDSE Economics syllabus. Using the midpoint method, the quantity change is 10 over an average of 25 (40%), and the price change is $2 over an average of $5 (40%), so PES = 1 and B is correct. The stem does not state the method, so it fits DSE level if students are expected to know the midpoint method, which is typically taught for elasticity.","picks":[]}

replies.en-18: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[3],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"The answer is B, (1) and (3) only. A unit tax raises the cost of supplying good Z, so the supply curve shifts vertically upwards by the amount of the tax, which makes statement (1) correct. Statement (2) is wrong because consumers and producers usually share the tax burden, with the split depending on the relative elasticities of demand and supply. Statement (3) is correct because the higher effective price reduces the quantity transacted.","picks":[]}
replies.en-22: {"intent":"new","drafts":[],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"","picks":[{"code":"C.pes","reason":"The request asks for a question on price elasticity of supply, which is the key point C.pes.","reasonZh":"要求是出一題關於供應價格彈性的題目，屬於 C.pes 供應價格彈性。"}]}
replies.en-23: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[2],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"Yes, B (1) is correct. Using the midpoint method, the change in quantity supplied is (30 − 20) / 25 = 40%, and the change in price is (6 − 4) / 5 = 40%. PES = 40% / 40% = 1, so supply is unitary elastic. The simple percentage method gives the same result: 50% / 50% = 1.","picks":[]}
replies.en-26: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[3],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"Statement (2) in Draft 3, 'Consumers bear the whole tax', is wrong because a unit tax is usually shared between consumers and producers. Consumers bear the whole tax only when supply is perfectly elastic, so producers receive the same price as before. The diagram isn't visible to me, so if it shows a sloped supply curve, the burden is split. The key B, (1) and (3) only, keeps the upward shift of the supply curve and the fall in quantity transacted, which are both correct.","picks":[]}
replies.zh-06: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[1],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"價格由 $10 升到 $12，升幅是 20%；需求量由 100 跌到 90，跌幅是 10%。需求價格彈性 = 10% ÷ 20% = 0.5，少於 1，所以需求缺乏彈性（inelastic），答案是 B。","picks":[]}

replies.zh-14: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[2],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"草稿 2 的題幹長度適中，只有一句引言、一個三欄供應表和一句問題，學生可以在短時間內讀完。表格數字已足夠計算 $4 至 $6 之間的供應價格彈性，所以不需要額外資料。如果你想再精簡，可以考慮把表格改成文字描述，但現時的長度對 DSE 題目來說並不算長。","picks":[]}
replies.mx-04: {"intent":"ask","drafts":[2],"how":"change","parts":[],"reply":"答案係 B（1）。用中點法計算：價格由 $4 升至 $6，中點為 $5，變動 2，即 2/5 = 40%；供應量由 20 增至 30，中點為 25，變動 10，即 10/25 = 40%。PES = 40% ÷ 40% = 1，屬單位彈性供應。","picks":[]}
